description:
The server and web UI use the core's repository construction, search and document operations. A refresh shares one issue capture across clients and API projections, and the browser consumes the graph instead of downloading complete issue descriptions on every change.

## Background

The shared bootstrap and issue-search entry point already exist in `commands/bootstrap.rs` and `commands/search.rs`. Server startup still discovers its own worktree; layout binding silently ignores a mismatched data root. The watcher already uses `VirtualPath` constants, but owns its own predicate and ignores configuration changes. Issue and graph handlers independently list issues, execute blocking work on async workers, and do not reuse results between clients.

The API still searches serialized issue JSON with ripgrep, while the browser separately scores downloaded issues. Document content/history/diff have parallel command methods; the Git epic owns version selection and storage Git primitives. The server also retains duplicate raw-response construction, response types and module declarations. The web's bulk layout and refresh passes repeatedly search arrays. Current facts and full consumer inventories belong in the linked investigation rather than historical byte counts or line snapshots here.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit-server` obtains its storage, repository layout and worktree paths from the same core constructor the CLI uses. The server crate makes no call of its own to layout or worktree discovery.
- [hard] REQ-02: Binding storage to a layout whose data root differs from the storage root fails with an error at construction, and server startup propagates construction errors before serving requests.
- [hard] REQ-03: The watcher's refresh predicate is one storage-owned allowlist built from the core storage path constants. The server crate contains no independently maintained storage file-name vocabulary.
- [hard] REQ-04: A change to `config.toml` emits a change event, and the web UI reloads hierarchy configuration on that event.
- [hard] REQ-05: The web UI makes no `/issues` request in response to a change event. Labels and dependency titles come from the graph response.
- [hard] REQ-06: One captured issue snapshot per tracker version feeds cached graph and base issue projections, irrespective of client count. The issue-list response applies live derived-document discovery without relisting issues, so artifact creation, deletion and rename remain visible after cache warm; configuration changes invalidate the cached projections.
- [hard] REQ-07: Every handler that reaches the executor goes through one helper. The helper runs blocking calls off async worker threads and maps errors through the shared classifier to HTTP status.
- [hard] REQ-08: One core semantic issue-search implementation serves `jit issue search` and HTTP issue matches, and the browser uses those matches instead of a client-side scorer. In the combined HTTP search, ripgrep supplies linked-document matches and never serialized issue-record matches. The distinct top-level `jit search` raw-content capability retains its documented file, glob and history scope.
- [hard] REQ-09: CLI and HTTP document content/history/diff operations call one core method set, and obsolete parallel methods are removed. The same selected document version returns identical bytes, including working-tree edits for unpinned documents. Supported HTTP diff is retained and uses the canonical core diff implementation.
- [hard] REQ-10: Verified unused routes `/status`, `/config/strategic-types`, `/changes`, `/gates/:key`, and unused web client methods, are removed. Supported `/issues`, `/health` and issue-document `/diff` remain. Server response types reuse core result types where their contracts coincide.
- [hard] REQ-11: The server binary uses the library's modules, so each server module compiles once and its tests run once. The server manifest declares no unused dependency.
- [hard] REQ-12: One shared response builder serves raw documents. MIME types come from `mime_guess`, and the server has one percent-coding implementation.
- [hard] REQ-15: Bulk graph layout and refresh passes resolve nodes and clusters through indexes built once per pass, without per-node array searches in `GraphView.tsx` or `clusterAwareLayout.ts`.

## Decisions

- D-1: Retire the MCP server completely and cleanly, as explicitly directed by the user and recorded in @/charter/D-23. REQ-13 and REQ-14 are retired from this epic without renumbering other criteria. A separately owned retirement task covers MCP source, packaging, release, documentation and test removal; this epic plans server/web work only.
- D-2: Retain `/issues` as a supported API projection and `/health` as the browser/deployment health surface. Retain HTTP document diff because its historical supported contract is sufficient to preclude speculative retirement. Absence of an in-tree caller alone does not prove an external API has no supported users; the explicit removal inventory in REQ-10 bounds the cutover.
- D-3: Reuse the existing command-owned issue-search entry point and shared bootstrap. Do not create competing implementations. The Git epic owns working-tree/pinned-version selection and Git primitives; this epic owns convergence of the remaining document adapters.
- D-4: The refresh contract is one shared issue capture, not one separate full read for each API projection. Indexing covers repeated layout/refresh passes; one-off event-handler lookups and the existing container-level selection policy are outside this change.

- D-5: Preserve top-level `jit search` as the documented raw-content search over repository data, including explicitly selected history. It is a different capability from semantic issue search. The HTTP/web combined search shares the core semantic issue matcher and linked-document ripgrep mechanism; this epic does not rewrite top-level search flags or retire raw search. Documentation distinguishes the two capabilities.

- D-6: Cache core issue data and graph projections, not the complete serialized `/issues` response. Its derived-document overlay reads configured artifact directories outside the data-root watcher and remains live without another issue listing. This preserves artifact visibility without adding dynamic multi-root watching.

## Notes

Serves @/charter/D-18 and @/charter/D-20. Document history and pinned reads consume the storage-owned Git mechanism under @/charter/D-21. Preserve @/inv/architecture-dependency-direction, @/inv/convention-convergence, @/inv/canonical-cutover, @/inv/orthogonal-tests and @/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint. The previously cited D-17 concerns mutation publication and is not the refresh-cost contract.
title: Run the server and web UI on the core's shared mechanisms
